Chapter 9: Overcoming Resistance and Building Resilience
Even when you're using all the right skills, resistance is just part of the process. You might notice people hesitate, push back, or even pull away when they feel pressure or start to feel unsure. But here’s an interesting perspective—what if resistance isn’t failure at all? What if it’s actually valuable feedback? It’s like a gentle nudge, telling you to pause, listen more closely, or maybe try a different approach.
So, how do you build resilience when you run into resistance?
First, stay curious. Ask open-ended questions and really listen. What’s making someone feel hesitant or uncomfortable? Dig beneath the surface.
Next, focus on validating feelings. When you acknowledge someone’s concerns without judging, you open the door to honest conversation. It’s about letting people know their emotions matter.
Another key is adapting your strategies. Be willing to change things up, try something new, or even pause when things aren’t working. Flexibility goes a long way.
And don’t forget the value of patience. Real change takes time, and trust is built step by step, through steady, respectful interaction.
Imagine a team leader rolling out a brand-new process. The team seems skeptical at first. Instead of pushing everyone to get on board right away, the leader could invite honest feedback, talk openly about concerns, and share stories of how similar changes worked out in the past. Over time, this approach helps build trust and gradually eases the resistance.
But here’s something we often overlook: building resilience isn’t just about managing others—it’s about taking care of yourself, too. Trying to influence people, especially when things are uncertain, can be exhausting. That’s why regular self-care matters. Whether it’s taking time to rest, reflecting on your experiences, or connecting with supportive friends, these habits help you recharge and keep your perspective.
So, the next time you hit a wall of resistance, remember—it’s not a roadblock, but a natural part of growth. When you meet resistance with empathy and a willingness to adapt, you not only strengthen your influence, but also deepen your relationships.
